papers.title: Minimum-Area Enclosing Rectangles and the First Neumann Eigenvalue of Planar Convex Domains
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded convex domain in the plane and let $R$ be a minimum-area rectangle containing $\overline\Omega$. We prove that if the ratio of the shorter side of $R$ to its longer side is at most $\rho \approx 0.443485$, then the first nonzero Neumann eigenvalue of $\Omega$ is bounded from below by that of $R$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $\Omega$ coincides with the interior of $R$. The proof is based on a flux identity for the means of a test function over vertical sections of $\Omega$, combined with weighted estimates involving the distributional second derivatives of the boundary functions. Finally, we show that the threshold $\rho\approx0.443485$ is nearly optimal by constructing, for every ratio in $(0.457994,1/2)$, trapezoids that are arbitrarily close to their minimum-area enclosing rectangle and for which the inequality fails.

papers.title: Uniform restriction lower bounds and nongeodesic common nodal curves in integrable systems
papers.abstract: We construct a family of real analytic metrics on the two-torus, for which a fixed embedded nongeodesic circle is a nodal component of infinitely many real Laplace eigenfunctions. The examples address a question asked by Bourgain-Rudnick \cite{BR11}, and give a negative answer to the question asked by Toth-Zelditch \cite{TZ21} and Han \cite{Han}: whether a curve shared by infinitely many nodal sets must be geodesic. To explain the restriction obstruction, we prove uniform $L^2$ lower bounds for joint eigenfunctions of quantum completely integrable (QCI) systems under transverse crossing and isolation of a tangential characteristic branch, then extend to multi-branch setting. The results are used to characterize the possible joint nodal curves in the Liouville tori, narrowing down the choices. Finally, the counterexample realizes one possibility for which cancellation happens exactly on a nongeodesic curve.

papers.title: On Mbekhta's conjecture and pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach and Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: We give negative answers to Mbekhta's conjecture \cite[p.~261]{Mbekhta} and to a related conjecture on pseudo-B-Fredholm operators \cite[p.~202]{AZO}. A sufficient condition for pseudo-Fredholmness on Banach spaces is established. It yields a characterization on Hilbert spaces in terms of the closedness of $\cc(T)$, $\cc(T)+\qn(T)$ and $\Ran(T)+\qn(T)$, as well as characterizations of pseudo-B-Fredholm and pseudo-B-Weyl operators on Banach spaces. A counterexample on a separable Banach space shows that the three closedness conditions do not characterize pseudo-Fredholmness in general. We also construct two operators having the same analytic core, quasinilpotent part, and kernels and ranges of all powers, although only one is pseudo-Fredholm. Moreover, a semi-B-Fredholm operator on a Banach space need not be a direct sum of a semi-Fredholm operator and a nilpotent operator, answering the question raised in \cite[p.~113]{AznayKato2023}. Finally, the three closedness conditions in the Hilbert-space characterization are shown to be independent.

papers.title: Entropy estimates and volume rigidity for graphs with positive Bakry-\'Emery curvature
papers.abstract: We establish a volume bound for weighted graphs with positive Bakry--\'Emery curvature through entropy estimates for the heat flow and characterize the equality case. As a consequence, if a connected unweighted graph $G=(V,E)$ satisfies the Bakry--\'Emery curvature--dimension condition $CD(2,\infty)$ with respect to the unnormalized Laplacian, then $$ |V|\le 2^d, $$ where $d$ denotes the maximum degree. Equality holds if and only if $G$ is a hypercube. We also establish an analogous volume rigidity result for the normalized Laplacian.

papers.title: Signed dual graphs and face spectral gaps of Cayley 2-complexes
papers.abstract: We construct a weighted signed dual multigraph for the Cayley $2$-complex of a finite presentation and represent its $\ell^2$ face Laplacian as a signed graph Laplacian with a diagonal potential. We prove that the face spectral gap above the kernel vanishes for the Baumslag--Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(1,m)$, $m\ge2$, using explicit finitely supported face chains. Our main vanishing theorem gives the same conclusion for every finitely presented amenable group with ordinary first Betti number at least two.

papers.title: P\'olya's conjecture for Neumann eigenvalues of annuli
papers.abstract: We prove strict P\'olya inequalities for every positive Neumann eigenvalue of every Euclidean annulus. The proof preserves the exact Weyl area term through a radial action identity and combines variational bounds with uniform Bessel-phase and angular-sum estimates. Explicit polynomial positivity arguments and angular-layer comparisons cover the remaining finite spectral ranges. We also obtain a positive counting surplus uniform in the radius ratio, an explicit subtraction of order $\sqrt{k}/(R^2-r^2)$ for all $k\ge1604$, and a positive square-root correction over the entire spectrum with a universal, non-explicit coefficient. The square-root order is sharp, and the first positive pair and the low-energy count admit optimal constants expressed by the first positive zero of $J_1'$. Neumann inequalities for annular products and congruent annular sectors follow by established transfer principles.
